manifest.name: dsh-protect-generated-files
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin that stops hand edits to generated files (lockfiles, protobuf/codegen output, files marked @generated or DO NOT EDIT) and tells the model which source to edit and what to run instead.
manifest.author: acus9345

bundle.text:
# dsh-protect-generated-files: no hand edits to lockfiles and generated code.
# To change settings, add a row like the one below to
# ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml (one profile) or ~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml
# (every profile). Keys you leave out keep their defaults.
#
# - id: protect-generated-files
#   config:
#     mode: deny                         # or ask
#     extraGlobs: { 'src/api/client/**': 'edit openapi.yaml and run npm run gen:api' }
#     ignore: ['vendor/**']              # never treat these as generated
#     defaultGlobs: true
#     guardShell: true
- insert:
    - id: protect-generated-files
      name: dsh-protect-generated-files

readme.text:
English | [中文](README_zh.md)

Agents edit files that nobody should edit by hand. They'll patch a version number straight into `pnpm-lock.yaml`, fix a typo in `user.pb.go`, or "correct" a type in Prisma's generated client. The edit looks fine until the next `pnpm install` or `protoc` run wipes it out, or, worse, leaves the lockfile disagreeing with `package.json` in a way that takes an afternoon to untangle.

This [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin refuses `write` and `edit` calls on generated files and lockfiles. It also refuses in-place shell edits of them (`sed -i`, `perl -pi`, `> file`, `tee file`). Instead of a bare "no", the model is told how the file is supposed to change:

```
dsh-protect-generated-files blocked this edit to db/query.sql.go: its header says it is
generated (`// Code generated by sqlc. DO NOT EDIT.`). A hand edit will be overwritten
the next time it is regenerated, or leave it out of sync with its source.
Instead: edit the SQL queries/schema and run `sqlc generate`.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-protect-generated-files
```

That's the `web` profile, the browser UI you start with `dsh web`. If you run DSH another way, use `headless` (scripts and CI) or `acp` (editor integrations) instead. Each profile keeps its own plugin list, so add it to every profile you use. It's active right after installing. Remove it with `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-protect-generated-files`.

To try local changes, build a tarball and install that:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/acus9345/dsh-protect-generated-files
cd dsh-protect-generated-files
npm install
npm pack

readme.section: How it decides a file is generated
readme.text: **Lockfiles, by name.** `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock(b)`, `deno.lock`, `Cargo.lock`, `go.sum`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock`, `pdm.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`, `composer.lock`, `mix.lock`, `pubspec.lock`, `Podfile.lock`, `flake.lock`, `gradle.lockfile`, `packages.lock.json`, `conan.lock`. Each one comes with the right command for its own package manager, for example "change dependencies with `cargo add / cargo update -p <crate>`".

readme.section: How it decides a file is generated
readme.text: **Known output paths.** Protobuf output (`*.pb.go`, `*_pb2.py`, ...), Dart `build_runner` output, `.Designer.cs`, minified files and source maps, and anything inside `node_modules/`, `__generated__/`, `.venv/` or `site-packages/`. Build-output folders (`dist/`, `target/`, `.next/`, `vendor/` and so on) only count when they sit next to a project manifest like `package.json`, `Cargo.toml` or `go.mod`, so a source folder that happens to be called `target` isn't caught.

readme.section: How it decides a file is generated
readme.text: **A header that says so.** It reads the first 15 lines of the file and looks for `Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT`, `@generated`, `DO NOT EDIT`, `auto-generated`, `This file was generated`, `<auto-generated>`, or a `Generated by <tool>` comment. A header that says the file may be edited ("edit freely", "safe to edit"), or a qualified `DO NOT EDIT without ...`, doesn't count. When the header names a tool it knows, the hint names that tool too: protoc/buf, Prisma, GraphQL Codegen, OpenAPI generators, sqlc, `go generate`, Drizzle, Alembic, and others. "Generated by hand" and "generated by ChatGPT" don't count.

readme.section: How it decides a file is generated
readme.text:
The header check only applies to files that already exist. The name and path rules also cover new files, because a lockfile written by hand from scratch is just as wrong.

On Windows, where DSH runs commands through PowerShell, it also watches `Set-Content`, `Add-Content`, `Out-File` and `Tee-Object`.

readme.section: When a hand edit is right
readme.text: It happens: resolving a lockfile merge conflict, or a one-line hotfix in vendored code while you wait for upstream. The model is told it can repeat the identical call once to confirm, and that goes through. Use `mode: ask` if you want to approve these yourself. If a directory is generated-looking but actually hand-maintained, add it to `ignore`.

The easy way: open **Plugins** in DSH's sidebar, click **dsh-protect-generated-files**, change what you want and press **Save**. It applies to the next tool call, no restart needed.

Or add a row like this to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, or to `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` for every profile. Keys you leave out keep their defaults.

```yaml
- id: protect-generated-files
  config:
    mode: deny                    # or `ask` for an approval prompt
    extraGlobs:                   # your own generated paths, each with the hint the model gets

`extraGlobs` is the one most worth setting. Telling the model which script regenerates your code saves it from guessing.

```sh
npm install
npm test           # detector unit tests
npm run test:e2e   # real dsh runs against a scripted local model, no API key needed
```

The install test runs `dsh plugin add`, which needs `pnpm` on your PATH.
